hero.title: Long-distance couples: the questions to ask, and the test that answers
hero.description: 20 questions drawn from 100 to see where your long-distance relationship stands: communication, visits, trust, shared plans. You answer on your own, and the result is immediate.

intro.p1: Can love really survive the miles? In 2026, this question has never been more relevant. With the rise of remote work, international student mobility, and dating apps that connect us across the globe, the boundaries of love have exploded.
intro.p2: Yet, when you find yourself alone at night facing a screen, the worry is there. "Are we wasting our time?", "Is he/she faithful?", "Is our story solid?". You're not alone in asking these questions.

section1.title: What is a long-distance relationship?
section1.sub1P1: Forget the classic image of the sailor going to sea for six months without news. In 2026, a long-distance relationship (LDR) is defined by two emotionally committed partners, geographically separated by a constraint that prevents regular physical intimacy.
section1.sub1P2: It's no longer just about kilometers, but about connection frequency. With current technology (HD video calls, instant messaging, augmented reality), you can "be" together without "being" there.
sub2Items: Global careers: People no longer hesitate to take that dream job in Berlin or Singapore.
Studying abroad: Exchange programs create thousands of couples every year.
Remote work and Digital Nomads: Geographic freedom allows travel, but sometimes schedules don't align.

section2.title: Statistics and trends 2026
section2.p1: Recent data estimates that about 14 to 15 million people in the United States consider themselves in a long-distance relationship. In Europe, the figure is also rising.
section2.sub1Text: In France, the culture of independence plays a key role. French long-distance couples often highlight preserving their personal space as an asset. The average time before reuniting geographically is around 18 to 24 months.

items.title: Strengthening emotional bonds
items.text: When you can't touch, you must talk. Really talk. Long-distance couples learn about each other's fears, dreams, and deep thoughts much faster.

items.title: Personal growth & autonomy
items.text: You get the best of both worlds: the emotional support of a couple, and the freedom of a single person in daily life.

items.title: Better communication
items.text: It's mathematical: to survive, you must communicate your intentions. This constant effort creates outstanding communicators.

items.title: Rituals and relationship creativity
items.text: Constraint creates creativity. Watching a movie "together", sending surprise packages, cooking the same recipe on video call... These rituals become the glue of your couple.

items.title: Loneliness and lack of physical contact
items.text: This is challenge #1. No hug after a hard day, no hand to hold at the movies. This "skin hunger" can create intense loneliness, even if you're virtually connected.

items.title: Jealousy and insecurity
items.text: "Why isn't he answering?", "Who's that girl on his story?". At a distance, imagination is your worst enemy. When that doubt really settles in, the question becomes does he or she still love me.

items.title: Uncertainty about the future
items.text: Ambiguity is toxic. "When will we live together?". Without a clear answer, motivation crumbles.

items.title: Financial and logistical pressure
items.text: Love is priceless, but train and plane tickets have a price. Managing trips, time zones, and budgets can create significant fatigue.

section5.title: What couples go through
section5.testimonial1: "We spent two years long-distance between Paris and Montreal. Our secret? We viewed the distance as a 'common enemy' to defeat together, not as a problem between us."
section5.testimonial2: "For us, the distance revealed cracks. The lack of shared projects turned the relationship into a polite friendship before fading. Love isn't enough, you need a shared direction."

section6.title: Signs your long-distance relationship can work
signs: Sincere and regular communication - You dare to say "I feel lonely today"
Mutual trust and commitment - Built through actions, not just words
Shared projects and clear goals - An end date, even vague, must exist
Ability to manage uncertainty - You turn frustration into reunion excitement

tips.title: Set a roadmap
tips.text: Always have the date of the next visit set before parting. It's the lighthouse in the night.

tips.title: Use technology intentionally
tips.text: Prioritize quality moments (a real video date) over empty quantity.

tips.title: Handle difficult moments together
tips.text: If one is struggling, the other must be present. Active listening is worth all the gifts in the world.

tips.title: Maintain intimacy
tips.text: In 2026, it's no longer taboo. Maintaining tension and intimacy at a distance is vital for many couples.

section8.title: Mistakes to avoid in a long-distance relationship

errors.title: Constantly comparing
errors.text: Don't envy the couple arguing at IKEA on Saturday. Your relationship is different, with its own superpowers. Comparison is the thief of joy.

errors.title: Unrealistic expectations about visits
errors.text: If you demand to see each other every two weeks when your budget doesn't allow it, you create financial pressure that will kill the relationship. Be realistic.

errors.title: Neglecting your personal life
errors.text: Don't put your life on hold. If you spend your evenings waiting for a call, you'll become dependent and uninteresting. Live for yourself!

section9.title: Where is the future of long-distance relationships heading?
section9.sub1Text: AI is beginning to play a mediating role. Apps now analyze sentiment in messages to avoid textual misunderstandings. Mixed reality headsets allow "dates" in ultra-realistic virtual worlds.
section9.sub2Text: Society in 2026 values the individual. We're more accepting of each person pursuing their dreams without sacrificing the couple. The "live together at all costs" model gives way to "be happy together, no matter where".

conclusion.title: Conclusion
conclusion.p1: A long-distance relationship is a colossal challenge, but it's also an incredible accelerator of emotional maturity. If you're reading this, it's because you care about your story. Distance is exhausting, but it doesn't explain everything: when the doubt is about the relationship itself, it helps to know what actually makes a relationship toxic.
conclusion.p2: There's no magic long-distance test that will give you a score out of 100, but there's your gut feeling. If trust is there, communication flows, and you have a reunion plan, then yes, it can work. And often, the reunions are all the sweeter.

items.q: What makes a successful long-distance relationship?
items.a: It's a relationship where both partners feel secure, loved, and free, despite the miles. It's characterized by a known and accepted end date for the distance.

items.q: How long does a long-distance relationship last on average?
items.a: Statistically, the "distance" phase lasts on average between 14 and 24 months before a decision is made: either geographical reunion (moving) or breaking up.

items.q: LDR: How to know if it's worth it?
items.a: Take stock: does this person bring you more joy than sadness? Do your life values align? If yes, distance is just a temporary logistical detail.

items.q: What are the 10 signs your long-distance relationship is solid?
items.a: If you laugh together, plan the future, trust each other, and each have your own fulfilling social life, you're on the right track.

items.q: Why do long-distance relationships fail (and how to avoid it)?
items.a: They often fail from lack of shared vision (no end date) or exhaustion (too many trips, not enough budget). To avoid it: communicate your limits and make a realistic financial and time plan.

results.fragileDesc: Distance may be complicated for you.
results.moderateDesc: You have a foundation but some areas need work.
results.readyDesc: You have the qualities needed to manage the distance.

section10.title: 18 questions to ask each other on a video call
section10.intro: The test above gives you a verdict. This list is for something else: pulling it out on a night when the call is running out of steam, when you've already covered your day and there are twenty minutes left to fill. Pick one at random.
section10.sub1Title: The everyday you never get to see
section10.sub1Text:
• Describe yesterday to me, but only the five most ordinary minutes of it.
  • What do I have absolutely no idea about in your flat?
  • Who have you seen this week that I've never met?
  • What do you do in the evenings when we're not on a call?
  • What habit have you picked up since we've been apart?
  • What makes you think of me on an ordinary day?
section10.sub2Text:
• What do you miss most, apart from actually seeing me?
  • Which moment of the week is the hardest?
  • Is there a subject you avoid bringing up on the phone?
  • What has the distance made easier between us?
  • When did you doubt this, even for five minutes?
  • What do I do that reassures you without me realising it?
section10.sub3Text:
• The first thing we do when we see each other again: you choose.
  • Honestly, how much longer before we're in the same city?
  • What would make you say this isn't worth it any more?
  • What are you dreading about the day we live together?
  • Which single-person habit are you not willing to give up?
  • If one of us had to move for the other, who would it be?
section10.outro: One rule if you want this to work: answer first, ask second. Otherwise one of you ends up sitting through a job interview.
